sec: Proximal (type 2) RTA: defect and causes · p822

items.q: Renal tubular acidosis type 2 is defined as:
opts: Isolated failure of the distal H⁺-ATPase
items.exp: RTA type 2 = generalised dysfunction of the PCT (proximal RTA). (Book p822)

items.q: Match the type 2 RTA defect — 1) Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger defect  2) Carbonic anhydrase defect  3) Overall description … A) Generalised dysfunction of the PCT  B) Enzyme defect  C) Exchanger defect
items.exp: The defect in type 2 RTA is a Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger defect and/or a carbonic anhydrase defect. (Book p822)

items.q: In childhood, type 2 RTA is caused by Fanconi's syndrome. Which is the most common underlying cause?
items.exp: Childhood causes: Fanconi's syndrome — cystinosis (m/c), Lowe's disease, and Wilson disease in adolescence. (Book p822)

items.q: Match the childhood causes of type 2 RTA to their age label — 1) Cystinosis  2) Lowe's disease  3) Wilson disease … A) Labelled adolescence  B) Most common cause  C) Also listed under Fanconi's syndrome
items.exp: Cystinosis is the m/c childhood cause, Lowe's disease is listed alongside it, and Wilson disease is tagged as adolescence. (Book p822)

items.q: A 16-year-old with tremor, Kayser–Fleischer rings and a proximal renal tubular acidosis — which printed cause fits best?
items.exp: Wilson disease appears under the childhood/Fanconi causes of type 2 RTA and is specifically tagged ‘adolescence’. (Book p822)

items.q: Match the adults' causes of type 2 RTA — 1) Haematological cause  2) Antiviral drug  3) Antibiotic … A) Gentamicin  B) Myeloma  C) Tenofovir
items.exp: Adult causes: myeloma and drugs — tenofovir, cyclophosphamide, outdated tetracycline and gentamicin. (Book p822)

items.q: Which quartet of drugs is printed as a cause of adult type 2 RTA?
items.exp: Drugs causing type 2 RTA in adults: tenofovir, cyclophosphamide, outdated tetracycline and gentamicin. (Book p822)

items.q: ‘Type 2 RTA is an isolated defect of bicarbonate reabsorption with everything else in the PCT working normally.’
opts: False — it is a generalised dysfunction of the PCT, so phosphate and glucose handling also fail
True — only the Na⁺–HCO₃⁻ exchanger is ever affected
True — that is why there is no glycosuria
False — type 2 RTA spares the PCT and affects the distal tubule only
items.exp: Type 2 RTA is a *generalised* PCT dysfunction: bicarbonate, phosphate and glucose handling all fail, hence rickets-like changes and glycosuria. (Book p822)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed causes of type 2 RTA. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Sjögren's syndrome is the acquired cause of *distal* RTA; type 2 RTA's causes are Fanconi's syndrome (cystinosis m/c, Lowe's, Wilson) and myeloma/drugs (tenofovir, cyclophosphamide, outdated tetracycline, gentamicin). (Book p822)
